final_transcript: Sorry I kept you waiting. That's AI chips, every day, waiting for data. And you, Sky, you pay full price to wait. So first, why change? Ofcom says traditional TV fell by 12 in a year as people move to streaming. Netflix and YouTube already know what you want to watch, so Sky needs that too, and fast. Second, why now? Well, you've already started with SkyQ voice search. Now, the next step is an AI assistant that knows each household. Imagine asking, Sky, make me scared. Third, why DDN? Idle chips will still cost you, and Cast AI found that enterprise chips average around 5 of use. It's like paying for a whole Sky Sports bundle just to watch Arsenal lose. Now, DDN's Infinia keeps data flowing to the chips, and they say customers reach up to 99 busy and cut costs per token by 75%. Plus, they already work with media companies like Canal Plus and Starz. So the arcs is clear. Let DDN run a pilot on the AI behind your voice search or your next assistant. Then measure the values before and after. And if both improve, scale it. So Sky. Don't be the next blockbuster. Thank you.
